newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares resume bull trend, Bombay up 1.55 pct.
newsitem.headline: India shares resume bull trend, Bombay up 1.55 pct.

text.p: ** Indian blue chips stage late rally, buoyed
by foreign fund buying in front-line stocks
** Bombay share index ends 62.23 pts, or 1.55 pct, higher
at 4,087.64, near day's highest level
** Market mood firm after ruling United Front coalition
defers a hike in government-set oil prices
** State Bank of India, ITC leads rally at Bombay bourse
after Monday's profit-taking
** National exchange index up 9.10 pts at 1,138.80, Delhi
gains 17.59 pts at 865.23, Madras 77.25 pts at 4,128.46
A last-minute surge in index-linked stocks drove up Indian shares to finish with smart gains in a day of choppy trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
Renewed buying by foreign funds in multinational companies coupled with a speculative rally in shares of tobacco giant ITC is likely to lead to a firm Wednesday opening, they said.
"A lot of money is coming in from abroad," said Dilip Joshi, dealer at Bombay brokers K.J. Shah. "Also, there is a lack of selling at lower levels."
The rally in blue chips reversed Monday's profit-taking after the market rose in the previous four sessions.

Among individual stocks, India's largest cement maker Associated Cement Companies (ACC) is expected to report sharply lower net in the year ended March due to spiralling input costs and an oversupply in major markets, analysts said.

"Volumes were flat during the year. On the other hand the company was faced with falling realisations and the rising cost of inputs like coal and power," said Jitendra Sriram, cement analyst at HSBC B&K Securities.
The firm is due to release its 1996/97 (April-March) results on Wednesday. ACC shares ended 66.75 rupees up at 1,215.75 at the Bombay exchange despite the lower forecasts, traders said.
"Funds are pursuing the same batch of stocks such as Hindustan Lever, Mahindra & Mahindra and TELCO," said the head of dealing at a foreign brokerage in Bombay.

Market reaction to the government's postponement of a hike in petroleum product prices was mixed, with some players saying that despite the short-term optimism, the government had proved unable to take hard decisions.

The ruling United Front coalition which met late on Monday said the issue of the mounting oil subsidy bill had been deferred until a meeting on June 27. It was the second time in three weeks that the coalition failed to reach consensus. -- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
